verdict.rationale: YYLO accepts a plain-language task description through `yylo init --task "Describe one verifiable outcome"` and runs it with a subagent. It can also pull Slack messages or GitHub issues into its kanban as tasks, and `task start` gives each task its own scoped branch/worktree. No evidence shows it automatically converting free-form intent into a refined, scoped implementation spec; the user writes the task framing. Missing for 10: documented automatic intent-to-spec conversion (scoping, acceptance criteria, decomposition) and any hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have it automatically turned into a scoped implementation task

citations.quote: yylo init --task "Describe one verifiable outcome" --subagent claude
Bring Slack messages or GitHub issues into kanban and return completed responses to their source thread.
`task start` freezes the protected target SHA, creates a dedicated branch/worktree, and completes configured dependency hydration before reporting `WORKING`.
